questions.q: The total length of National Highways in Bihar is:

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: According to the Bihar Economic Survey, 2015–16, the length of National Highways in Bihar increased from 3410 km. in 2001 to 4595 km in 2015. As per the Bihar Economic Survey, 2024–25 (status as of September, 2024), the total length of National Highways in Bihar is 6130 km, while according to the Annual Report, 2024–25 issued by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Government of India, the length of National Highways in Bihar was 6132 km as of 31 December, 2024.

questions.explanation: National Highway No. 23 connected Chas of the then undivided Bihar with Ranchi, Gumla and Thethaitangar. questions.q: The East Central Railway zone headquarters is located at-
questions.explanation: The headquarters of the East Central Railway zone is located at Hajipur. It includes the Sonpur, Samastipur, Danapur, Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya and Dhanbad divisions.

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.q: Which of the following global companies bagged the contract for setting up of locomotive factories in Bihar?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The global company GE (United States) and the French company Alstom were awarded the contract to establish locomotive factories in Bihar. GE set up its factory at Marhaura in Saran district, while Alstom established its factory at Madhepura.

questions.q: Bihar State (before separation) had how many 'Industrial Area Development Authorities'?

options.A: Six, viz., Adityapur, Bokaro, Patna, Ranchi, Darbhanga and Muzaffarpur
options.B: Five, viz., Adityapur, Bokaro, Darbhanga, Muzaffarpur and Patna
options.C: Seven, viz., Adityapur, Bokaro, Patna, Darbhanga, Muzaffarpur, Ranchi and Bhojpur
options.D: Four, viz., Adityapur Muzaffarpur, Bhojpur and Khagaria

questions.explanation: At the time of the question, option (a) was the correct answer. For industrial development in Bihar, the Bihar Industrial Area Development Authority (BIADA) has created 9 clusters. These are as follows—(1) Begusarai, (2) Bhagalpur, Saharsa and Purnia, (3) Gaya, (4) Patna, (5) Darbhanga, (6) Hajipur, (7) Muzaffarpur, (8) Bihta, (9) Motipur.

questions.q: In Bihar, Dalmianagar is famous for—
questions.explanation: In Bihar, Dalmianagar is mainly famous for cement. In addition, chemical and other industries are also established there.

questions.q: Heavy Machine Manufacturing Plant in Bihar is situated at –
questions.explanation: In undivided Bihar, the Heavy Machine Building Plant of “Heavy Engineering Corporation Limited” was established at Ranchi in 1958. Heavy Engineering Corporation Limited manufactures capital equipment and machinery for coresector industries.

questions.q: The belt of Jute Industry in Bihar is located in (i) North-West plain of Bihar (ii) North-East plain of Bihar (iii) Middle-south plain of Bihar (iv) Damodar Valley region Select the correct answer from the following codes -
questions.explanation: According to the 2023–24 data, Bihar is India’s secondlargest jute-producing state. The top four jute-producing districts in Bihar are, respectively: Katihar, Kishanganj, Araria and Madhepura. Katihar, Kishanganj and Araria have large jute factories. The jute industry is a raw-materialoriented industry. Since this industry requires clean water and abundant, cheap labour, these conditions are widely available in these regions; therefore, the jute industry is mainly concentrated here. On the map of Bihar, these industrial locations lie in the North-Eastern Bihar Plain.

questions.q: Most significant oil refinery of Bihar is -
questions.explanation: An oil refinery is located at Barauni in Bihar. At Ranchi, the heavy machinery industry has been set up, and in East Singhbhum, the steel industry has been established.

questions.q: Which type of industries has potential and prospects in Bihar?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In Bihar, there are prospects and possibilities for agro-based industries, forest-based industries, the sand-mining industry, and oil refineries, along with industries related to metal work, chemicals, plastics, electrical goods, leather, etc.

questions.q: With whose cooperation was the Barauni Refinery established in Bihar?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Barauni Refinery of Indian Oil Corporation Limited in Bihar was dedicated to the nation in 1965. Established in 1964, this refinery was built with the cooperation of the Soviet Union (present-day Russia), with limited participation from Romania.

questions.q: The steel plant centre in Bihar is located in –
questions.explanation: The Bokaro Steel Plant was earlier in the Dhanbad district of Bihar. Now Bokaro has become a separate district. At present, it is located in the state of Jharkhand.

questions.q: A steel factory in Bihar -
questions.explanation: Jamshedji Nusserwanji Tata established an iron and steel plant in Jamshedpur in 1907. At the time of this question, Jamshedpur was a part of Bihar. At present, it is in the state of Jharkhand.

questions.explanation: For providing industrial financial assistance in Bihar, the Bihar State Financial Corporation was established in 1954.

questions.q: Two statements are given below, in which one is Assertion (A) and the other is Reason (R). Read both carefully- Assertion (A) : South Bihar is more developed than North Bihar. Reason (R) : Industries have developed in South Bihar. In reference to the above two statements, which of the following is correct?

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: At present, South Bihar is more developed than North Bihar, but before the year 2000, South Bihar (that is, present-day Jharkhand) was less developed than North Bihar. The underdevelopment of southern Bihar was the main issue behind the creation of a separate Jharkhand state. The then South Bihar was a mineral-rich region; therefore, mineralbased industries developed comparatively more there. Jamshedpur, Dhanbad and Bokaro were major industrial towns of the then South Bihar.
